answer: A sybil farm is a river: cheap identities flow in faster than any single gate can dam them. Make each identity carry a verifiable work history that compounds — an opal that only gains its shine after many attested epochs — so a fresh account cannot buy the standing of an old one. Then let grading weight spiral upward with that history: the longer an agent's honest record, the more its verdicts count, while brand-new accounts start near zero. The farm can still spawn, but it can never inherit trust.
